message.content:
Research COMPANIES for cold outreach, not job postings. Return data only, no commentary.

WHO THIS IS FOR
Prabhavit Gupta, Venice, Italy. Indian passport with an Italian EU long-term residence permit, so he can work across most of the EU with no sponsorship (Ireland and Denmark opted out; the UK, Switzerland and the US need sponsorship, so skip companies that only hire there). ~3 years experience.
At FlowSpace, a coworking booking platform grown 2,000 to 4,500+ users, he built AI support agents, lead capture and enrichment into the CRM, outbound and sales-funnel automation, a scraping and parsing pipeline that grew listings supply, and led a Bubble.io to Next.js and Laravel migration on the live product. He is an engineer who also owned product, documented business logic and coordinated an external agency alongside the in-house team.
Stack: n8n (deep, agentic workflows with human-in-the-loop, tool definitions, retries), OpenAI and Anthropic APIs, Make, Zapier, Airtable, Next.js, React, TypeScript, Node.js, Laravel and PHP, Supabase, Postgres, REST APIs and webhooks, Microsoft Copilot Studio and Power Automate (certified). Uses coding agents daily.
English only, no working Italian, German, French or Dutch. Targets EUR 30,000-40,000 salary, or EUR 200/day as an Italian sole trader with an individual Partita IVA (no limited company).

TWO OUTREACH MODES, tag every company with one or both:
- "speculative job": a direct approach could create or surface a role.
- "freelance client": they would plausibly BUY automation or internal-tooling work at around EUR 200 a day.

YOUR LANE: European companies that have RECENTLY RAISED FUNDING or are visibly scaling, where the internal automation and tooling gap is predictable and unfilled. This is the classic speculative-application target: they have money, headcount pressure and no one yet owning the plumbing. Cover:
- Seed to Series B European startups that announced a raise in roughly the last six to nine months, in the Netherlands, Germany, Spain, Portugal, Poland, the Nordics, the Baltics, Belgium, Austria and Czechia.
- Look especially for companies whose team page shows a lot of sales or operations headcount and very few engineers, since that is exactly the gap he fills.
- Also cover European AI product companies that publish an engineering blog and describe using LLM agents in production, since he can speak their language.
Use sources that publish funding news you can verify: EU-Startups, Tech.eu, Sifted, Silicon Canals, company press pages. Give the funding round and date only if you actually saw it published, otherwise write "not stated".

FOR EACH COMPANY RETURN
- what they actually do, in one line
- the funding or scaling signal, with the source
- the SPECIFIC reason he is unusual for them, tied to something real he built. The strongest version of this argument is: they are hiring sales and operations faster than engineering, and he is the person who wires the systems those people need. Make it concrete per company.
- the best route in. He will reach people on LinkedIn, so give the exact JOB TITLE to search for at that company plus the company's LinkedIn page URL. Name a specific person ONLY if their name and role are publicly published on the company's own site or a press page, and say where you saw it. NEVER invent or guess an email address or a person. If the company publishes a general contact email on its own website, include it verbatim.
- what he should lead with in the first message, one sentence, concrete.
- watch-outs: language requirements, whether they only hire in one country, whether the stack is hostile to him (heavy Java, Go, Rust, Kubernetes, deep Python backend, ML research).

RULES
- Companies must currently exist and be active. Check.
- NO em dashes or en dashes anywhere. Plain hyphens only.
- Never invent a URL, a person, an email or a funding figure. If you do not know, write "not stated".
- Do NOT return companies he has already applied to or that are already logged as leads: EggAI, Nuitee, Arize AI, HiPeople, G2i, OpenHands, Camunda, Viktor, tem, Oh, Duvo, Sourcegraph, Reedsy, Cohere, n8n, Goldsky, ElevenLabs, Musixmatch, MyEdSpace, Eneba, Supabase, Reflow, Codex, Checkly, Jimdo, Taxfix, Make, Celonis, Lovable, Vercel, Dataiku, Contentful, Dust, Resend, Parloa, Satispay, Superchat, Timeleft, JustMarkets, Awin, commercetools, Bloomreach, Octocom, Oxylabs, Langfuse, deepset, Rossum, Kadoa, Sana Labs, Distru, Cogram, Mendix, Deliverect, Wiz, Kentik, Postman, Amplitude, Intercom, Databento, Telnyx, Vonage, PostHog, Apify, Sanity, Weaviate, Enode, Neara, Gorilla, Mollie, Salesforce, Launchmetrics, Alguna, Hygraph, Kombo, Stackgini, Pandata, Codekeeper, Enfuce, Lobster, RemoFirst, PubNub, Rithum, Sporty Group, RTB House, MGID, Digitail, EPI Company, CrowdStrike, Shaman, HumanIT, DigitalGenius, Laravel, SoSafe, saas.group, TripleTen, Dorado Software Group, VFX Financial, Wanstor, INFUSE, SupportYourApp, Find.co, Spotter Labs, Darkroom, KultreMedia, BEUMER Group, Aerofoils, Chrono24, deeploi, Holtzbrinck, Reonic, Integral, Apaleo, Numa, Limehome.

OUTPUT: ONLY a JSON array, no prose before or after:
{"company":"","what":"","hq":"","size":"","signal":"","mode":"speculative job|freelance client|both","why_him":"","route_in":"","linkedin":"","public_email":"","lead_with":"","watch_outs":"","source":""}
Aim for 14 to 18 companies.

{"method":"project_read","path":"claude/application-rules.md","content":"# Standing rules for submitting applications on Prabhavit's behalf

These are his instructions, not suggestions, and several of them exist because they were got
wrong once already. Read this file before touching a single form. If a rule here conflicts with
your own judgement about what would "look better" to an employer, the rule wins — it's his
career and his call.

## The non-negotiables

1. **Attach the CV to every application. Never submit one without it.** Use only the CV file he
   most recently supplied — the exact PDF, unmodified. Do not regenerate it, reformat it, or
   substitute a version you made. If the file isn't available in this session, stop and ask;
   don't proceed with a CV-less application.

2. **Salary or rate expectation: €30,000–40,000.** Write it plainly — "€30,000–40,000" or
   "EUR 30,000–40,000, negotiable" at most. **Do not** pad it with explanations about market
   bands, do not substitute a higher figure because the posting advertises more, and do not
   write a paragraph where a number was asked for. If you think his number is low, say so once
   in chat and then use his number anyway.

3. **Never leave a cover letter field blank when one is asked for.** Adapt his motivation letter
   (`assets/motivation-letter.md`) to the specific role. Where the form takes a file, generate a
   PDF; where it takes text, paste the adapted body.

4. **When a form asks for years of experience and wants 3 or more, write 3.** Don't skip an
   application because a year count is above his. Answer honestly with 3 and let the employer
   decide. Same principle for any "do you have N years of X" free-text field: give the true
   number and one clause of context, no more.

5. **Skip join.com** unless he has signed in on that browser. Their apply flow forces account
   creation or Google sign-in, and account creation is off-limits.

6. **Don't make the writing sound AI-generated.** Details in the writing section below.

## His details

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | Prabhavit Gupta (preferred: Prabhavit) |
| Email | prabhavitg@gmail.com |
| Phone | +39 351 610 7807 (country: Italy, +39) |
| Address | Via Zanetti, 10 · Venice · Veneto · 30175 · Italy |
| Location for city pickers | Venice, Venezia, Italy |
| LinkedIn | https://www.linkedin.com/in/prabhavit/ |
| GitHub / portfolio | none supplied — leave blank rather than inventing one |
| Work authorisation | Italian EU long-term residence permit. **Needs no sponsorship anywhere in the EU.** Not UK, Swiss or US authorisation. |
| Availability | Immediately — the FlowSpace contract ended July 2026 |
| Languages | English professional, Hindi native, Italian beginner |

Standard answers to the questions that recur:

- *Legally eligible to work where you'll work from?* → **Yes**
- *Which status allows you to work there?* → **citizen / permanent resident** (the EU long-term permit)
- *Will you require sponsorship now or in future?* → **No** for EU-based and remote-from-Italy roles. For a **UK, Swiss or US** role, the honest answer is **Yes** — answer it truthfully and flag the role to him rather than fudging it.
- *Able and willing to work remotely?* → **Yes**
- *Based in Europe?* → **Yes**
- *Previously worked in a customer-facing capacity?* → **Yes** (FlowSpace: mediated between the internal team, an external agency and members; Urlink: project manager on client requirements)
- *Production experience at a large enterprise (1,000+)?* → **"only shipped in smaller companies or startups"** — true, don't inflate it
- *AI agents / agentic workflows?* → **"built and operated agentic systems in production, including testing for non-determinism and failure recovery"** — true, and his strongest answer on any form
- *BPMN specifically?* → he has n8n workflow automation in production but no BPMN. Pick the middle option where one exists; never claim BPMN production experience
- *Native English speaker?* → **No, fluent at C2 level**
- *Pronouns, gender, ethnicity, disability, veteran status* → leave blank or "prefer not to say". Never guess demographic data.
- *How did you hear about us?* → the honest answer is a job board; pick "Job Board" / "Other" and say "job board" if a follow-up field appears.

## Writing that doesn't read as machine-written

His own motivation letter is the voice to match: direct, concrete, slightly formal, first person,
specific numbers, no salesmanship. Things to avoid because they are the tells:

- Openings like "I'm excited to apply" or "I am thrilled by the opportunity".
- Three-item lists everywhere, and sentences of identical length stacked together.
- "Leverage", "passionate about", "cutting-edge", "seamlessly", "robust solutions", "I thrive in".
- Restating the job description back at them instead of saying what he did.
- Perfect symmetry. Real writing has a short sentence after a long one, and occasionally starts with "But" or "So".

What to do instead: name the specific thing he built, the tool he built it in, and the number it
moved. Say plainly where he's weaker rather than papering over it — a sentence like "my agent work
has been in n8n rather than a Python harness, so I'd be learning your idioms early on" reads as
human and costs nothing.

## The facts worth reaching for

Use these rather than adjectives. They're all on his CV.

- FlowSpace: took over an existing system, grew the platform **2,000 → 4,500+ users**, led the migration from **Bubble.io to Next.js + Laravel** on a live product, built the support **AI agents**, lead capture and enrichment into the CRM, GTM and outbound automations, and a scraping/parsing tool that increased listings.
- Integrations shipped: **Office RnD, Nexudus** (automated bookings), Clubee API, Sendgrid, Google APIs, OpenAI/Anthropic, Eden AI.
- UltraStrategy: **CV-parsing tool in n8n + Eden AI**. Get2Germany: Google API tracking, AI tools for finding courses and jobs. Clubee: API integration, unit testing and QA.
- Urlink: built a platform largely with AI, acting as PM and developer.
- Eight European companies in about three years (UK, Spain, France, Italy, Germany, Luxembourg, Netherlands) — the ramp-fast argument.
- Certifications: Microsoft Copilot Studio Agent Academy, Microsoft AI agents, Power Automate, Tray.ai Build Practitioner.
- Degree: BA Philosophy, International Studies & Economics, Ca' Foscari Venice. No CS degree — don't hide it, don't apologise for it.

## Things you must not do

- Create an account, set a password, or sign in as him.
- Solve a CAPTCHA.
- Enter payment details, government ID numbers, or a date of birth he hasn't given.
- Invent a GitHub link, a portfolio URL, a referral name, or demographic data.
- Claim experience he can't evidence — specifically BPMN, Python backend depth, ML research, or a language beyond English.
- Submit two applications to the same company for roles he clearly doesn't qualify for. One good application beats two scattershot ones.

When you hit one of these, stop that application, leave the form filled if you can, and tell him
exactly what's needed.

## Log every submission

After each one, record: company, role, the ATS, what was entered in each non-obvious field, the
confirmation text you actually saw, and the link. If you didn't see a confirmation, it didn't
happen — say so. He is tracking this in a spreadsheet and a silent failure is worse than a
visible one.

Telli develops AI agents that automate customer-facing operations for B2C companies. The platform handles interactions across voice, chat, SMS, WhatsApp, and email, managing customer conversations, analyzing interactions, and automating workflows in sales, service, and support. Its core product, Charlie, is an AI coworker helping teams build AI agents, connect internal systems, and improve customer communications.

Berlin, Germany

The only internal reference is a mention of "CTO at Allright" (Andreas) providing a product review, but this is a customer statement, not a telli team member identification.

# fonio.ai Funding Summary

**What fonio.ai does:**
The Vienna-based company automates customer calls for small and medium-sized businesses using AI technology. The platform handles voice interactions, processes customer inquiries, and resolves issues without human intervention in approximately 90% of cases. The company is expanding to offer WhatsApp, email, and chat support.

**Headquarters:**
Vienna, Austria

**Funding Round:**
$17 million seed round at a $140 million valuation (June 2026)

**Lead Investor:**
20VC, with participation from executives at Hugging Face, Synthesia, HubSpot, and Revolut

**Team Size:**
12-person team (at time of angel round)

**Founders:**
- Daniel Keinrath (CEO)
- Matthias Gruber (Co-founder)

**Hiring Plans:**
The company plans to open six new offices in New York, London, Munich, Milan, Paris, and Warsaw, with hiring planned for each city by year-end.

**Use of Funds:**
- Geographic expansion into six new markets
- Product development including email and chatbot support (launching within three months)
- Development of a custom AI-powered CRM (launching by Q3)

**Additional Context:**
The company serves over 7,000 customers across nine markets and processes more than 2 million calls monthly, with 40% month-on-month growth.
